name: XMonitor - Scheduled Post Tracking Staging
description: Inactive staging copy of the scheduled post tracking workflow using staging Supabase/Postgres/Telegram credentials and shared X/OpenAI credentials.

parameters.query:
WITH blocked AS (
  SELECT post_id
  FROM public."Posts"
  WHERE status IN ('Ignored', 'Snoozed')
),
advanced AS (
  UPDATE public."Posts"
  SET
    snooze_runs_remaining = GREATEST(snooze_runs_remaining - 1, 0),
    status = CASE
      WHEN snooze_runs_remaining <= 1 THEN 'New'
      ELSE 'Snoozed'
    END
  WHERE status = 'Snoozed'
  RETURNING post_id
)
SELECT COALESCE(array_agg(post_id), ARRAY[]::text[]) AS blocked_post_ids
FROM blocked;

-- Every candidate post (10+ replies) is stored now, not only threshold crossers,
-- so a running denominator exists for posts that have not crossed yet.
-- Alerting is gated downstream on alert_now.
INSERT INTO public."Posts" (
  post_id,
  post_text,
  comment_count,
  negative_count,
  status,
  user_id,
  created_at,
  snooze_runs_remaining,
  analyzed_count,
  negative_ratio
)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, 'New', $5, now(), 0, $6, $7)
ON CONFLICT (post_id) DO UPDATE
SET
  post_text      = EXCLUDED.post_text,
  comment_count  = EXCLUDED.comment_count,
  negative_count = EXCLUDED.negative_count,
  user_id        = EXCLUDED.user_id,
  analyzed_count = EXCLUDED.analyzed_count,
  negative_ratio = EXCLUDED.negative_ratio
-- created_at is deliberately not reset: candidate posts are refreshed every pass
-- and resetting it would make every stored post look newly discovered.
-- status is deliberately not touched, so Ignored/Snoozed survive a refresh.
RETURNING post_id, post_text, comment_count, negative_count, status, user_id, created_at, snooze_runs_remaining, analyzed_count, negative_ratio;

-- Hidden vs visible counts over ALL stored negative replies for the post,
-- not just the ones fetched this run. Matches the denominator convention in
-- CLAUDE.md: stored analyzed negative replies.
WITH requested AS (
  SELECT unnest($1::text[]) AS post_id
)
SELECT
  requested.post_id,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.reply_id IS NOT NULL AND lower(COALESCE(r.status, 'New')) =  'hidden')::int AS hidden_negative_replies_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.reply_id IS NOT NULL AND lower(COALESCE(r.status, 'New')) <> 'hidden')::int AS non_hidden_negative_replies_count
FROM requested
LEFT JOIN public."Replies" r
  ON r.post_id = requested.post_id
 AND r.sentiment = 'Negative'
 AND r.analyzed_at IS NOT NULL
 AND r.deleted_on_x_at IS NULL
GROUP BY requested.post_id;

nodes.name: Probe OpenAI Error Reason
nodes.notes: Runs only when the sentiment call failed. One minimal request so the raw OpenAI error code (credits vs rate limit) is visible to the alert builder.

nodes.name: Build Sentiment Failure Alert
nodes.notes: Classifies an OpenAI sentiment failure (credits vs rate limit vs other) and shapes it for the scheduler developer alert.

parameters.query:
-- Ensure the marker row exists and return it together with this run's start time.
-- last_successful_run_at is advanced only at the end of a successful pass.
INSERT INTO public."Run State" (key, last_successful_run_at)
VALUES ('scheduled_post_tracking', NULL)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET key = EXCLUDED.key
RETURNING key, last_successful_run_at, now() AS run_started_at;

nodes.name: Get Run State
nodes.notes: Reads the last successful pass timestamp that bounds the replies query, and stamps this run's start time.

parameters.query:
SELECT COALESCE(array_agg(reply_id), ARRAY[]::text[]) AS analyzed_reply_ids
FROM public."Replies"
WHERE analyzed_at IS NOT NULL
  AND post_id = ANY($1::text[]);

nodes.name: Get Analyzed Reply Ids
nodes.notes: Replies already scored in an earlier pass. These are dropped before the OpenAI call so each reply is analyzed once.

nodes.name: If Has New Replies
nodes.notes: No new replies means nothing to score. Skip OpenAI entirely and just advance the run state.

parameters.query:
-- Running per-post totals from replies scored in earlier passes.
-- The new replies from this run are added on top in Calculate/Filter Sentiment Counts.
WITH requested AS (
  SELECT unnest($1::text[]) AS post_id
)
SELECT
  requested.post_id,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.analyzed_at IS NOT NULL)::int                                AS stored_analyzed,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.analyzed_at IS NOT NULL AND r.sentiment = 'Negative')::int    AS stored_negative,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.analyzed_at IS NOT NULL AND r.sentiment = 'Positive')::int    AS stored_positive,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE r.analyzed_at IS NOT NULL AND r.sentiment = 'Neutral')::int     AS stored_neutral
FROM requested
LEFT JOIN public."Replies" r ON r.post_id = requested.post_id
 -- Replies deleted on X are kept for history but are no longer part of the conversation.
 AND r.deleted_on_x_at IS NULL
GROUP BY requested.post_id;

nodes.name: Get Stored Post Counts
nodes.notes: Supplies the stored half of the negative ratio denominator.

parameters.query:
-- Reached only once every fetched reply is stored with its sentiment.
-- The OpenAI failure path never reaches this node, so an aborted pass
-- leaves the marker untouched and the next run re-reads the same window.
UPDATE public."Run State"
SET last_successful_run_at = $1::timestamptz,
    updated_at             = now()
WHERE key = 'scheduled_post_tracking'
RETURNING key, last_successful_run_at;

nodes.name: Advance Run State
nodes.notes: Advances the incremental watermark. Uses the run START time, so replies created mid-run are not skipped.

parameters.query:
-- Quiet pass: the replies query returned nothing new, which is a successful
-- outcome, so the watermark still advances.
UPDATE public."Run State"
SET last_successful_run_at = $1::timestamptz,
    updated_at             = now()
WHERE key = 'scheduled_post_tracking'
RETURNING key, last_successful_run_at;

nodes.name: Advance Run State (Quiet Pass)
nodes.notes: Terminal node for the no-new-replies path.

nodes.name: Build Media Classify Requests
nodes.notes: One multimodal request per reply carrying media. Emits a single no_media sentinel when this pass has none, so the chain never stalls on an empty branch.

nodes.name: If Has Media Replies
nodes.notes: Routes past the multimodal call when this pass found no media replies.

nodes.name: Classify Media Replies
nodes.notes: One multimodal call per media reply. Throttled and non-fatal: a failure leaves the reply on its text-only label.

nodes.name: Apply Media Sentiment
nodes.notes: Overrides the batched text label with the multimodal label, for media replies only. Emits the same shape the sentiment node did, so downstream counting is unchanged.

nodes.name: If Fetch Truncated
nodes.notes: True when a search stopped on the page cap rather than on an exhausted next_token.

nodes.name: Build Truncation Alert
nodes.notes: Turns a silent page-cap truncation into a visible developer alert.

parameters.query:
-- Active labelling rules, at most one row per client (enforced by
-- sentiment_cheat_sheets_one_active_idx). Drafts are excluded: they wait for
-- human activation before they can influence production labelling.
SELECT
  client_id::text AS client_id,
  version,
  rules_text
FROM public."Sentiment Cheat Sheets"
WHERE status = 'active';

nodes.name: Get Active Cheat Sheets
nodes.notes: One active cheat sheet per client. alwaysOutputData is on: an empty table must not stall the analysis path.

parameters.query:
-- T3: tracked users carry their client's alert thresholds, so every downstream
-- decision is made per client instead of against a constant.
--
-- "Clients" is JOINed but NOT filtered on c.is_active: deactivating a client must
-- not silently stop collecting its posts. An inactive client is dropped at delivery
-- instead -- see Get Alert Recipients -- so the data keeps flowing and only the
-- Telegram fan-out stops.
--
-- Both Supabase projects are shared with the sibling FB Monitor project, so every
-- table is named explicitly.
SELECT
  tu.user_id,
  tu.username,
  tu.display_name,
  tu.telegram_chat_id,
  tu.is_active,
  tu.client_id::text            AS client_id,
  c.slug                        AS client_slug,
  c.name                        AS client_name,
  c.min_replies::int            AS client_min_replies,
  -- numeric would arrive as the string '0.50' and break a strict-typed compare.
  c.negative_threshold::float8  AS client_negative_threshold,
  c.lookback_days::int          AS client_lookback_days
FROM public."Tracked Users" tu
JOIN public."Clients" c ON c.id = tu.client_id
WHERE tu.is_active
ORDER BY tu.user_id;

nodes.name: Get Tracked Users
nodes.notes: T3: joins "Clients" so each tracked user carries its client thresholds.

parameters.query:
-- T3: recipients resolved per post owner. This replaces the unfiltered read of
-- "Telegram Users", which handed every recipient every client's post text and
-- reply counts the moment a second chat existed.
--
-- A chat receives a post only when it is an active, alert-receiving member of the
-- client that owns that post.
--
-- LEFT JOIN, not INNER, on purpose: a client that has alerting posts but no
-- eligible member must still produce a row, so Build Negative Alert Notification
-- can raise a developer alert naming it rather than dropping the alert in silence.
-- c.is_active is applied here, so a deactivated client stops receiving Telegram
-- alerts while its posts continue to be collected and stored.
--
-- "Telegram Users" is deliberately no longer read. The Telegram router still
-- writes it, so the table stays in place; retiring it is a later cleanup.
WITH requested AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT unnest($1::uuid[]) AS client_id
)
SELECT
  requested.client_id::text AS client_id,
  c.name                    AS client_name,
  c.slug                    AS client_slug,
  cm.chat_id,
  cm.label,
  cm.role
FROM requested
LEFT JOIN public."Clients" c
  ON c.id = requested.client_id
 AND c.is_active
LEFT JOIN public."Client Members" cm
  ON cm.client_id = c.id
 AND cm.is_active
 AND cm.receives_alerts
ORDER BY requested.client_id, cm.chat_id;

nodes.name: Get Alert Recipients
nodes.notes: T3: replaces the unfiltered "Telegram Users" read. The router still writes that table; it is simply no longer a routing source.

parameters.query:
-- Posts whose replies were already collected in an earlier pass.
--
-- A post NOT in this list is a first-time fetch: it only became a candidate once its
-- X reply_count crossed the client's min_replies, so every reply it already had is
-- older than the watermark window. Build Replies Query gives those posts a backfill
-- window starting at the post's own created_at instead.
SELECT COALESCE(array_agg(DISTINCT post_id), ARRAY[]::text[]) AS collected_post_ids
FROM public."Replies"
WHERE analyzed_at IS NOT NULL
  AND post_id = ANY($1::text[]);

nodes.name: Get Backfilled Post Ids
nodes.notes: Which of this pass's candidate posts already have replies stored. Anything missing here is being fetched for the first time and needs a window starting at the post's own created_at, not the run watermark.

parameters.query:
-- Refreshes only posts already stored; never inserts. status, snooze state and
-- the sentiment counters are deliberately untouched.
WITH m AS (
  SELECT * FROM json_to_recordset($1::json) AS x(
    post_id text, reply_count int, like_count int, retweet_count int,
    quote_count int, bookmark_count int, impression_count int)
)
UPDATE public."Posts" p
SET comment_count      = COALESCE(m.reply_count, p.comment_count),
    like_count         = COALESCE(m.like_count, p.like_count),
    retweet_count      = COALESCE(m.retweet_count, p.retweet_count),
    quote_count        = COALESCE(m.quote_count, p.quote_count),
    bookmark_count     = COALESCE(m.bookmark_count, p.bookmark_count),
    impression_count   = COALESCE(m.impression_count, p.impression_count),
    metrics_updated_at = now()
FROM m
WHERE p.post_id = m.post_id
RETURNING p.post_id, p.status, p.comment_count, p.like_count, p.metrics_updated_at;

-- Shared classifier prompts, one row set per Supabase project (X, FB and IG all
-- read this table). Composed by Resolve Sentiment Prompts. A failed read stops the
-- run on purpose: no labels from an unknown prompt.
SELECT key, system_prompt, user_template, model, temperature::float8 AS temperature, categories, updated_at
FROM public."Sentiment Prompts"
ORDER BY key;
